To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-17 activates the Act1/TRAF3IP2/MyD88 complex to mediate the IL-17 signaling, which is negatively regulated by the ubiquitin ligase TRIM63 and the E3 SUMO ligase PIAS3.

Act1, the cytosolic adaptor of IL-17, plays a critical role in IL-17 signaling by recruiting and assembling the signal transducing molecules and by regulating the ubiquitination of the signaling molecules.

IL-17 receptor signaling is mediated by Act1, and that Act1 regulates IL-17 signaling in multiple ways, including the activation of NF-κB pathway and the stabilization of TNFα induced gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how IL-17 signaling is regulated by the adaptor molecule Act1, and the role of the IL-17 signaling in the pathogenesis and treatment of autoimmune diseases and cancers
the activation and regulation of the signaling pathway mediated by IL-17 receptor (IL-17R).
the regulation of IL-23/IL-17 axis, and the role of Act1 in this regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL-17/Act1 signaling is a highly regulated process that involves a large number of signaling molecules and regulatory mechanisms.
Act1 is a key adaptor protein for IL-17 signaling and that Act1 is the master regulator in the IL-17 mediated signaling.
IL-17 signaling is a complex process involving multiple molecules and pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Act1 is the central hub for IL-17 signaling and its activity is regulated in a complex manner by a number of factors including IL-17, TNFα, TGFβ, and IL-1.

Act1 plays a central role in regulating the signaling of IL-17 and other cytokines including IL-6, IL-21, IL-27 and IFNγ, and that the regulation of Act1 is a critical mechanism for the regulation of IL-6 and IL-17 signaling pathways.
Act1 is a critical mediator of IL-7 signaling and is regulated by multiple mechanisms to control IL-17 mediated immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-17 signaling is tightly regulated by Act1 and its associated proteins.
IL-17 receptor (IL-17R) signaling can be regulated by several mechanisms including the phosphorylation of Act1, the ubiquitination of Act1, and the ubiquitination and phosphorylation of IL-17R.
Act1 plays multiple roles in IL-17 receptor (IL-17R) mediated signaling.
